parts.note: read plainly, just a catalogue reference to one of the nine symphonies
the setter wants its popular title, from the composer's own countryside heading

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses run this clue into the next two, which give the ninth and third symphonies by their nicknames.
explanation.definitionFit: The F major work of 1808 depicts country life, a brook, peasants dancing and a thunderstorm, hence its rural title.

parts.note: read plainly, the last of the composer's numbered symphonies
the setter wants its nickname, from the singers who join in the finale

explanation.walkthrough: 'His' points back through the ellipsis to Beethoven in the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The final symphony brings in soloists and a chorus singing Schiller's Ode to Joy, giving it its familiar label.

parts.note: read plainly, simply the composer's symphony number three
the setter wants its Italian title, meaning heroic, first dedicated to Napoleon

explanation.walkthrough: 'His' again means Beethoven, carried over by the ellipsis from 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The E flat symphony of 1804 was published under an Italian title celebrating the memory of a great man.

parts.note: read plainly, anything associated with the cold season
the setter means the white flakes of frozen water that fall from clouds

explanation.definitionFit: Frozen crystals falling from the sky and settling on the ground are the classic material of cold weather.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a common female first name
second meaning: a spinning firework, or a round window with radiating spokes

explanation.walkthrough: The wheel is named after Saint Catherine of Alexandria, said to have been sentenced to die on a spiked wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The saint's name is both a popular female forename and the label for a pinwheel firework or rose window.

parts.note: read plainly, a place higher up
the setter means the idiom for having control or advantage over someone

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes having the advantage or control in a contest, as in gaining it over a rival.

parts.note: read plainly, any sports hall or fitness centre
the setter means the full Greek-derived name for such a hall

explanation.definitionFit: The word for an indoor hall equipped for athletic training comes from the ancient Greek place where athletes trained.

parts.note: read plainly, a verb meaning to put something down
the setter means the noun for a particular location

explanation.definitionFit: A particular point or small area, as in a nice picnic location, is a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: read plainly, any way of getting about
the setter means the network of tracks carrying trains

explanation.definitionFit: Train lines and their rolling stock form one of the main systems for moving passengers and freight.

parts.note: read plainly, any seabird seen in rough weather
the setter means the small ocean bird linked by sailors with bad weather

explanation.walkthrough: The storm species was thought by sailors to herald gales; its name may come from Saint Peter walking on water.
explanation.definitionFit: These tubenosed ocean birds patter over waves and were believed by mariners to foretell gales.

parts.note: read plainly, a phrase about something missing
the setter means the single adjective for someone away or missing

explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing from school or work is described with this adjective, the opposite of present.

parts.note: read plainly, a sense of kinship with others
the setter means the Greek-derived word for sharing another's sorrow

explanation.definitionFit: Compassion and shared emotion for another person's troubles is the standard synonym, from Greek roots meaning suffering together.

parts.note: read plainly, any dwelling built in Alpine fashion
the setter means the wooden mountain cabin with wide overhanging eaves

explanation.definitionFit: A timber Alpine cottage with a sloping roof and deep eaves, now also used for ski holiday lodges.

parts.note: read plainly, any drink made by steeping plants in hot water
the setter means the French word for a herbal tea

explanation.definitionFit: Herbal teas such as camomile or mint, steeped in boiling water, go by this French-derived name.

parts.note: read plainly, possibly the noun for a sound-deadening panel
the setter means the verb for puzzling or bewildering someone

explanation.definitionFit: To confuse or bewilder someone completely is the shared sense of these two verbs.

parts.note: read plainly, any oversized sewing implement
the setter means the blunt, thick-eyed tool for threading tape or cord

explanation.definitionFit: A thick blunt implement with a big eye is used for drawing tape, ribbon or elastic through hems.

parts.note: read plainly, any town along that river
the setter means the large city where the Saône joins it, in its French spelling

explanation.walkthrough: The French spelling is wanted, not the English form with an S.
explanation.definitionFit: France's third-largest city sits at the confluence of two major rivers in the southeast of the country.

explanation.definitionFit: Potassium aluminium sulphate fixes colours to fabric as a mordant and helps cure leather hides.

parts.note: read plainly, any of the composer's thirty-two piano works in that form
the setter means the nickname of the C sharp minor piano sonata

explanation.walkthrough: The nickname came after the composer's death, from a critic who compared the first movement to a lake at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano Sonata No 14 gained its popular title from a critic likening it to Lake Lucerne by night.
